world-scholars-cup-bucharest-round-2027.about:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).

This is a regional round in Bucharest, Romania, on 6–7 April 2027, hosted by International School of Bucharest. Students can join through a school club or as an independent team of three from any country; results can qualify teams for a Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.
highlights: Four team events: debate, collaborative writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for a Global Round and the Yale Tournament of Champions
world-scholars-cup-bucharest-round-2027.eligibility: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; independent teams are welcome. Divisions: Senior (born on or before 1 July 2013) and Junior (younger); scholars must be born on or before 31 December 2016.
how_to_apply: Form a team of three (school club or independent)
Open the WSC registration portal and choose this round (or use the round's Request Info link)
Register the team and any accompanying adults, and pay the fee by card or bank transfer
Study the 2026–27 theme and curriculum before the round
Attend the round in Bucharest, 6–7 April 2027
world-scholars-cup-bucharest-round-2027.costs: Registration fee per scholar (student): regular 70 EUR, late 80 EUR. Adults/coaches register separately; travel, accommodation and most meals are extra. Payment by card or bank transfer through the WSC portal.

Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).
